correctness.rationale: The universal reduction uses the materially inspected theorem that every Reinhardt polygon with fewer than 30 sides is periodic. For n=9, the possible repetition divisors and positive odd-length blocks give exactly the regular class and [(3)^3]. The latter is reconstructed geometrically from a unit-side equilateral triangle and three three-chord subdivisions of 60-degree unit-circle arcs; exact cap decomposition gives its area. The regular area follows from diameter normalization and the regular-polygon formula. The area gap is algebraically simplified and proved positive by a triple-angle comparison. The packaged SymPy checker independently replays all coordinate and finite-classification calculations.

value.rationale: The nonagon is the first odd Reinhardt side count with a nonunique maximum-perimeter optimizer. Area is the other classical diameter-normalized extremal objective studied in the same literature, making area on the tied perimeter-extremal set a natural secondary invariant. The result completely resolves that secondary problem, not merely one example: it gives both possible exact areas and their exact positive separation.
